address: 105 Edwards Village Blvd Unit# 4957, Edwards, CO
areas: Vail and the Vail Valley, Colorado

hero.eyebrow: For homeowners in the Vail Valley
hero.sub: Paths, trees, and stonework lit after dark, so the house feels safe and warm and your evenings outside run longer. Brass and copper fixtures made for Vail winters.

items.p: Stone, timber, and trees lit from the right angle, so the house reads from the road and the drive after dark.
Patios, outdoor kitchens, and fire pits you keep using after sunset, with light where you sit and eat.
Paths, stairs, and the front walk lit so no one trips, and the property looks watched when you are away.

about.p: Mark is a partner of Lighthouse Outdoor Lighting in Vail, with a background in landscape architecture and design and installation work across several regions. His goal is to create visual works of art in any environment, with a strong dedication to customer service.
about.alt: Mark Nall with his black dog on a rocky ridge above the Vail Valley

steps.p: We walk the property with you, listen to the goals, and find the vantage points that matter.
A lighting plan with revisions, value engineering, and a working timeline so the budget and schedule hold.
A project manager runs the install, closes with a 20 point inspection, then the designer aims every fixture at night.
Legacy Care keeps the system tuned as the landscape grows and the seasons turn.

items.p: Mark with Lighthouse did an amazing job on my home. I did not install exterior lighting when I built the house, so Mark had to find some unique ways to make my house shine.

Mark was so helpful with is ideas and was able to create exactly what we were looking for. He was prompt, courteous and professional. He stopped by numerous times after the installation to make sure everything was perfect.

Mark has a great eye for outdoor lighting design and landscaping. His lighting recommendations not only enhances the beauty  but increases security. Mark is very reliable and knowledgeable. Love his lighting designs and his strong work ethic.

items.q: Why light the landscape at all?
items.a: Lit paths and steps keep people safe, lit stone and trees show the house at its best, and a lit property is worth more.

items.q: What kind of lighting works best in Vail?
items.a: Low voltage LED, in layers: soft light on decks and paths, stronger light on trees and stonework.

items.q: What fixtures last in the mountains?
items.a: Brass and copper. They shrug off corrosion, age well, and blend into the natural surroundings.

items.q: How often does a system need service?
items.a: Snow, wind, and wildlife take a toll, so a yearly checkup keeps it at its best. Our Legacy Care plans cover that.

items.q: Can lighting help plan the yard?
items.a: Yes. Light marks out the zones: the paths, the seating, the garden beds, and the kitchen, so the whole yard works after dark.

items.p: Sound designed to go with the lighting, for a quiet evening or a full party on the patio.
Preventive maintenance that keeps the lighting and audio performing night after night.
The season or a special event lit with the right equipment, your feet kept on the ground.

final.p: Tell us about your home and pick a time for a design consultation.

footer.creds: Mark Nall: B.A. Landscape Architecture, Berkeley. MBA, University of Colorado.
